title: Complexity of simple abstract systems imposes fundamental limits on proof

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complexity of simple abstract systems imposes fundamental limits on proof

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The complexity found in simple abstract systems leads to fundamental limitations on mathematical proof, of the kind hinted at by Gödel's Theorem, and these limitations are relevant well beyond the narrow scope of current mathematics.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 1: The Foundations for a New Kind of Science

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: one of the consequences of this complexity is that it leads to fundamental limitations on the idea of proof that has been central to traditional mathematics.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 1, “The Foundations for a New Kind of Science”; section “Relations to Other Areas” (from p. 7), p. 7. Scope: mathematical proof applied to abstract systems based on simple programs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch01-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.77

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Standard mathematical constructions can establish rigorous proof limitations in simple abstract systems. The expansive claim about consequences beyond mathematics is not fully captured by those theorems.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Formalize a sufficiently expressive class of simple program systems and prove undecidability or incompleteness for propositions about their behavior. Such theorems establish fundamental proof limitations for that class, while broader relevance must be assessed separately.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Relevant well beyond current mathematics is not sharply delimited.

Undecidability of a class does not make every instance unprovable.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Universality of a simple rule is published, and undecidable questions about that rule follow by the usual reduction. That is the Gödel-like half of the claim, and it is checkable. The further assertion that these limits matter well outside existing mathematics is a judgment about relevance, and neither the proof nor any dataset decides it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From a universality proof for a simple system, derive a concrete undecidable question about that system, such as whether a given finite pattern ever appears. That settles the existence of Gödel-like limits inside simple programs. It does not settle whether those limits are relevant well beyond the current scope of mathematics.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Undecidability of one encoded question does not measure how often ordinary mathematical questions are blocked.

Relevance beyond the current scope of mathematics has no formal or empirical decision criterion.
